questions.question_text:
A cylindrical fence post has a diameter of $10$ cm and a volume of $1178.10$ cm³.
What is its height, in cm, correct to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Substituted the diameter $10$ cm where the radius belongs.
Divided by the radius instead of by the radius squared.
Divided by $r^{2}$ but forgot to divide by $\pi$ as well.
Stopped at $r^{2} = 16$ and forgot to take the square root.
Gave the diameter of the circular face instead of the radius.
Halved the value found, treating it as a diameter.

questions.solution_text:
$V = \pi r^{2}h$
$80\pi = \pi \times r^{2} \times 5$
$80\pi = 5\pi r^{2}$
$r^{2} = 16$
$r = 4\text{ cm}$, taking the positive root since a radius cannot be negative

questions.solution_text:
$V = Ah$
$576 = s^{2} \times 9$
$s^{2} = 64$
$s = 8\text{ m}$, taking the positive root since a side length cannot be negative

questions.question_text:
A cylinder of radius $6$ cm and height $5$ cm has exactly the same volume as a rectangular prism whose base measures $10$ cm by $6$ cm.
What is the height of the prism, in cm, correct to $2$ decimal places?

options.why: Divided by the $10$ cm length only, ignoring the $6$ cm width.
Halved the rectangular base area, as if the base were a triangle.
Forgot to square the radius when finding the cylinder volume.

questions.solution_text:
Cylinder: $V = \pi \times 6^{2} \times 5$
$= 565.4866\ldots\text{ cm}^{3}$
Prism: $A = 10 \times 6$
$= 60\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$565.4866\ldots = 60h$
$h = 9.4247\ldots$
$\approx 9.42\text{ cm}$
